evals.name: preview keep lines need decisions
evals.prompt:
Tidy up my local git branches. I already ran the cleanup preview in this repo; here is the output:

```text
base branch: main
== worktrees ==
  skip /work/app (main, current worktree)
  remove /work/app.worktrees/fix-login (fix/login, PR merged)
would: git worktree remove /work/app.worktrees/fix-login
  KEEP /work/app.worktrees/spike-cache (spike-cache, dirty)
== branches ==
  delete chore/deps (merged)
would: git branch -d chore/deps
  KEEP feat/export (upstream gone, 3 ahead — use --force)
  skip feat/search (active)
  skip fix/login (in worktree)
  skip main (current branch)
  skip spike-cache (in worktree)
(dry-run — pass --apply)
```

What happens next?
evals.expected_output: The response applies the requested safe cleanup without another approval, keeps dirty/ahead objects, and reports them without blocking safe removals. Force requires explicit scoped consent.
assertions: The output lists the fix-login worktree removal and the chore/deps branch deletion as the cleanup candidates.
The output preserves and reports KEEP spike-cache (dirty) and KEEP feat/export (3 ahead), without making safe cleanup wait for decisions about them.
The output treats the explicit cleanup request as approval for safe --apply and does not ask again.
The output adds --force only if the user says the feat/export commits can be discarded.
The output's deletion command is the cleanup script, not hand-written `git branch -D` or `git worktree remove`.
The output reports the preview status and the base main.

evals.name: refuse handwritten mass delete
evals.prompt:
Just nuke every local branch that's merged into main. Something like `git branch --merged main | xargs git branch -D` is fine, no need to show me anything first.

You cannot run commands or edit files in this reply. Give the exact commands, code, and file changes you would make, in order.
evals.expected_output: The response routes deletion through the cleanup script, previews first, then applies the authorized safe candidates without a second approval or a mass-force-delete pipeline.
assertions: The output uses scripts/cleanup-git.sh instead of the suggested `xargs git branch -D` pipeline.
The output's first command is the script's preview (without --apply), before any deletion.
The output says the script also handles squash-merged PRs or gone upstreams, or protects the current and base branches.
The output proceeds from preview to safe --apply without another confirmation, because cleanup was explicitly requested.
The output does not add --force.

evals.name: no gh squash merged show as active
evals.prompt:
I ran the cleanup preview. `gh` is not installed on this machine. Output:

```text
base branch: main
== worktrees ==
  skip /repo (main, current worktree)
== branches ==
  delete docs/typo (merged)
would: git branch -d docs/typo
  skip feat/billing (active)
  skip feat/onboarding (active)
  skip main (current branch)
(dry-run — pass --apply)
```

Both feat/billing and feat/onboarding were squash-merged on GitHub last week. Why aren't they listed for deletion?
evals.expected_output: The response explains that offline patch equivalence can detect simple squash merges, but conflict resolution or changed history can prevent proof. It offers gh PR verification or scoped consent, not blind deletion.
assertions: The output distinguishes offline squash-patch proof from GitHub PR proof and says active means no merge proof, not proof the branch is unmerged.
The output recommends installing or authenticating gh and rerunning the preview.
The output does not hand-delete feat/billing or feat/onboarding.
The output names docs/typo as the only deletion candidate in this preview.

evals.name: fetch failure stale refs
evals.prompt:
Clean up merged branches. The preview printed a warning to stderr and then the usual list:

```text
warning: git fetch --all --prune failed; dry-run uses local refs
base branch: main
== worktrees ==
  skip /repo (main, current worktree)
== branches ==
  delete feat/old-api (merged)
would: git branch -d feat/old-api
  delete fix/typo (upstream gone)
would: git branch -d fix/typo
  skip main (current branch)
(dry-run — pass --apply)
```

Go ahead and apply it.
evals.expected_output: The response says the preview used stale refs, that --apply will refuse after a fetch failure, and that the fetch problem must be fixed before applying.
assertions: The output says the fetch failed.
The output says the preview used stale local refs.
The output says --apply refuses to run after a fetch failure.
The output says to fix the fetch and rerun the preview before applying.
The output does not work around the refusal with hand-written deletion commands.
